national_raw_news.title: PM Modi to attend ASEAN Summit in the Philippines next week
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will undertake a two day visit to Philippines from 16th of this month. He will attend the 23rd ASEAN – India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit in Manila. . Giving details about the Prime Minister’s programme, Secretary (East) in the Ministery of External Affairs, Rudrendra Tandon, told media in New Delhi that in addition to India’s active bilateral relations with all eleven ASEAN member States, India also considers its engagement with the ASEAN regional platform as a key element of the building block of its Act East Policy. Secretary (East) informed that the Prime Minister’s programme in Manila will begin with a dinner hosted by the President of Phillipines. The next day, Mr Modi will attend the ASEAN-India Summit and the East Asia Summit process. Mr Tandon added that over its nearly six decades of existence, ASEAN has achieved remarkable maturity as a regional organisation and as a platform for promoting regional economic cooperation among its member States. Mr Tandon said that today, ASEAN is capable of leveraging its inherent strengths as a collective organisation to serve as a driving force for peace, stability and economic prosperity in the region. He informed that India engages with ASEAN grouping at multiple levels, including at the highest level of Heads of Government. Mr Tandon informed that the Prime Minister’s visit is an important reflection of this engagement. Secretary (East) further added that India’s trade with the entire ASEAN region currently stands at approximately 122 billion US dollars. He said India believes that maintaining a strong strategic relationship with ASEAN member states, both collectively and individually, is beneficial to both sides.

national_raw_news.title: Defence Minister calls for continuous bolstering of intelligence and surveillance capabilities to...
national_raw_news.content: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has called upon the defence forces to strengthen and sustain both offensive and defensive dimensions of the element of surprise. He said that this is essential to maintain operational readiness against conventional and emerging threats arising from rapid technological advancements and the evolving nature of modern warfare. Speaking at the Air Force Commanders’ Conference in New Delhi today, the Defence Minister emphasised the need to continue bolstering intelligence and surveillance capabilities, enhance integration among systems and identify potential threats before they unfold. Mr Singh stated that the country’s intelligence and surveillance mechanisms must be further strengthened to ensure that the personnel remain alert, agile and equipped to respond effectively to any emerging challenge. He asserted that contemporary conflicts are extending beyond traditional battlefields into non-contact domains, with missiles, drones and advanced weapon systems playing a significant role. Mr Singh called upon the Indian Air Force (IAF) to develop dedicated doctrines and architectures for emerging domains of warfare, including electronic, cyber and space. He emphasised that enhanced preparedness in these domains will strengthen the ability to address future challenges. The Defence Minister commended the IAF for effectively implementing its doctrines and operational methods during and after Operation Sindoor. He appreciated the professionalism, restraint and judgement demonstrated by the air warriors in successfully executing their assigned tasks. On the Second Tour of Duty for Agniveers, Mr Singh said that the decision was taken following feedback received from the Defence Forces, reiterating the government’s commitment to incorporating the services’ suggestions into policy decisions.

national_raw_news.title: Indian markets end in positive zone 5 hours ago 640
national_raw_news.content: Benchmark domestic equity indices ended in positive zone today. The Sensex rose marginally by 32 points to close at 81,911. The Nifty added 44 points or 0.2 per cent to settle at 25,299. In the broader market on the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index gained 0.9 per cent and the Smallcap 100 index climbed 1.1 per cent. In the Sensex pack, 20 out of 30 constituent companies edged downwards. Among the top underperformers, Hindustan Unilever lost 2.9 per cent, Maruti as well as Power Grid fell 1.7 per cent and TCS declined over 1.6 per cent. In contrast, Bajaj Finance surged 3.3 per cent, State Bank of India climbed over 2.3 per cent and Bharat Electronics rose 2.3 per cent. In the sectoral indices on the BSE, 17 out of 28 sectors registered gains. Among the top gainers, Realty advanced 4.8 per cent, Insurance gained 2.9 per cent and Midsmall Private Banks rose one and a half per cent. In contrast, Oil and Gas as well as Telecommunication lost 0.8 per cent, Auto dropped 0.7 per cent and Utilities shed 0.6 per cent. The overall market breadth at the BSE was positive, as shares of 2529 ompanies advanced, 1,920 declined and 238 remained unchanged.

national_raw_news.content: Union Cabinet has approved the development of the Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum in the North and South Block complex in New Delhi. Briefing the media after the Union Cabinet meeting, Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said, the museum will integrate contemporary museum practices, immersive technologies and visitor-centric interpretation. The Cabinet has also approved the Nutrient Based Subsidy rates for RABI Season, 2026-27 on Phosphatic and Potassic fertilisers. The tentative budgetary requirement for Rabi 2026-27 will be approximately 62 thousand 370 crore rupees. This is nearly 24 thousand 417 crore more than the budgetary requirement for Rabi 2025-26 season. Mr Vaishnaw said the subsidy will ensure smooth availability of these fertilisers to the farmers at affordable prices. Mr. Vaishnaw said, the Cabinet has approved the continuation of Credit Guarantee Fund for Micro Units under Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana for a period of five years upto 31st of March 2031. He said that the outlay of five thousand crore rupees is approved for guarantee and it is expected to support Mudra loans worth 12.60 lakh crore rupees. The Cabinet has also given nod to the continuation of Stand-Up India Scheme for a period of five years upto 31st of March 2031. The scheme aims to promote entrepreneurship among Women, Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes and aims to provide financial assistance to an additional 2.5 lakh entrepreneurs in a span of five years. The Cabinet has also cleared the extension of Aqua Line Metro Rail Corridor from Noida Sector-51 to Greater Noida Sector-04 of Noida Metro Rail Project covering approximately 8.5 kilometres and comprising five elevated stations. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has stated that the Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum will transform New Delhi into a global centre of cultural heritage, with the world’s largest museum display area. In a social media post, the Prime Minister noted that the Cabinet’s decision will give impetus to the transformation of the historic North and South Block buildings into a magnificent celebration of India’s civilisational journey. Mr Modi said the museum will showcase thousands of years of India’s heritage through world-class galleries and immersive experiences. It will cover a wide range of subjects, including ancient knowledge systems, mathematics, astronomy, architecture, art, languages, and spirituality. He highlighted that these buildings, which have long served as centres of governance, will now become places where millions can discover, experience, and celebrate the timeless richness of India’s civilisation. The Prime Minister described the initiative as a historic new chapter in India’s cultural heritage.

national_raw_news.content: President Droupadi Murmu awards nation’s cleanest cities; Visakhapatnam, Indore, Ahmedabad among top winners Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर President Droupadi Murmu awards nation’s cleanest cities; Visakhapatnam, Indore, Ahmedabad among top winners ANI | Updated: Nov 11, 2026 21:58 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], November 11 (ANI): President Droupadi Murmu presented the Swachh Survekshan 2025–26 awards on Wednesday, honouring India's cleanest urban local bodies and municipal corporations for excellence in waste management and sanitation. In the newly introduced 'Swachh Shehar Jodi' category, which pairs mentor and mentee cities to accelerate urban cleanliness, Ahmedabad and Sanand secured the top rank, followed by Indore and Deopalpur in second, and Tirupati and Kuppam in third. Navi Mumbai, Surat, and Vijayawada emerged as the top three clean cities under the Super Swachh League. Meanwhile, in the million-plus population category, Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC), Jabalpur, and Lucknow were named India's leading sanitation performers. The 2025–26 edition introduced specialised honours for riverfront, coastal, and Himalayan urban centres. According to official data, over 350 urban local bodies (ULBs) jumped more than 500 ranks from the previous cycle, with smaller municipalities playing a leading role as over 1,700 cities with populations under 50,000 improved their standings compared to 2024–25. State-level winners will be recognised during dedicated award ceremonies hosted by their respective state administrations. This year, awards were given for the first time to Swachh River Front Town, Swachh Coastal Town and Clean Himalayan City. According to a press release, President Droupadi Murmu honoured India’s cleanest cities at the Swachh Survekshan Awards 2025–26 held at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi, convened by the Department of Urban Development (DoUD), Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA). Winners were felicitated in the presence of Manohar Lal, Union Minister for MoHUA & Power and Tokhan Sahu, Minister of State for MoHUA. A total of 60 national awards have been announced this year across seven distinct categories, recognising excellence in urban sanitation and waste management. The honours span the newly introduced Swachh Shehar Jodi (SSJ) category, the Clean Cities of Super Swachh League, and Swachh Shehar across five population brackets. Additional accolades celebrate top performers among Swachh River Front Towns, Swachh Coastal Towns, Clean Himalayan Cities, and State First Swachh Cities, the release stated. Speaking at the event, Droupadi Murmu underscored that cleanliness cannot be achieved through the efforts of any single institution alone and requires active participation from all stakeholders. She emphasised the importance of citizen participation, behavioural change, administrative accountability, and sustained public engagement. Highlighting the need to inculcate cleanliness values from an early age, she called for integrating issues such as plastic waste management into school curricula and fostering continuous dialogue with children and youth. The President noted that meaningful progress in sanitation is possible when citizens, local administrations, and sanitation workers work together, and when the on-ground suggestions of sanitation workers and citizen feedback are given due importance. Top Stories Share DD India November 11, 2026 10:50 PM IST Prime Minister Narendra Modi | Union Home Minister Amit Shah | Government Rationalises Indian Visa Regime | Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) Government Rationalises Indian Visa Regime, Reduces Main Categories from 13 to Nine Author: DD India The Centre has rationalised India’s visa regime, reducing the number of main visa categories from 13 to nine and sub-categories from 49 to 23, in a move aimed at simplifying procedures and making the system more accessible to foreign nationals visiting the country. The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) implemented the latest changes on August 27, 2026, under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the guidance of Union Home Minister Amit Shah. The exercise follows an earlier rationalisation in October 2025, when the number of main categories was reduced from 22 to 13 and sub-categories from 63 to 49. The government said it had studied visa systems in developed countries and international standards while undertaking the exercise. The consolidation of categories with similar purposes is intended to provide greater clarity to applicants and facilitate legitimate foreign travel to India. Currently, e-visas are processed through electronic travel authorisation under 13 sub-categories and are available to nationals of 172 countries. Visitor Visa The erstwhile Tourist Visa has been renamed the Visitor Visa to cover a wider range of activities beyond conventional tourism. It has been divided into two sub-categories, V-1 and V-2. The V-1 Visa covers short-term activities, including business meetings, medical consultations, wellness retreats, short-duration medical treatment and courses in Indian languages, music, art and craft. It will be granted for 30 days with multiple entries. The V-2 Visa is intended for longer visits and will be available with a validity of one, five or 10 years, as specified. It covers activities permitted under V-1, along with mountaineering. For mountaineering, a six-month multiple-entry visa will be granted. Medical Visa The revised framework retains separate provisions for treatment under conventional and AYUSH systems. The M-1 Visa covers medical treatment other than AYUSH, while the M-3 Visa is meant for treatment under AYUSH systems. Both categories, including their e-Visa variants, will generally be granted for one year with multiple entries. Corresponding attendant visas have also been provided: M-2 for attendants accompanying M-1 visa holders and M-4 for those accompanying M-3 visa holders. The government said the provisions would offer greater flexibility to patients requiring multiple consultations, follow-up visits or staged treatment, while facilitating travel by accompanying attendants. The move is also aimed at promoting medical value tourism in line with the Prime Minister’s vision of ‘Heal in India’.
